transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what brings me in is... my supervisor told me I had to come. We were having this staff meeting the other day. It was Tuesday, actually, because they always bring in those powdered donuts on Tuesdays from the bakery down on 4th street. The one with the green awning, you know it? They make a really good apple fritter, too. 

Anyway, I got really worked up during the meeting. We were talking about safety, and I just started acting out a whole fall-prevention drill right there in the room. I was dragging chairs around, waving my arms to show how you gotta brace somebody if they go down... catching people is heavy work, you know? I'm a personal care aide, so I see it. My uncle slipped on some ice back in '09 and broke his hip, had to get a whole replacement. Those titanium hips are really something else, they set off the metal detectors at the airport every time he goes to Florida. 

But yeah, I was doing the drill with the chairs and my arms going everywhere, and I just couldn't seem to stop doing it. Even when folks were telling me to sit down and take a breath, I just kept going. So... they sent me here.
Lately, have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

Well, yeah, I guess so. I mean, lately I can sleep maybe two or three hours, and I'll wake up way before dawn just... completely ready to go. I don't think anything is wrong with being up while the house is still dark, just sitting there making all these big plans. It's actually the best time to think because it's so quiet. 

The only thing you hear is the paper delivery guy. He comes around 4:30 on this vintage Schwinn bicycle. I had a bike exactly like that when I was a kid, cherry red with the silver fenders. Man, we used to take those things off these sweet dirt jumps behind the old abandoned grocery store on Elm. Broke my collarbone on one of those jumps once, had to wear this awful sling for weeks. It itched like crazy in the summer heat. 

But yeah, I'll just be up in the dark, feeling fantastic, mapping out this whole new deck I want to build out back. You know the price of treated lumber is just through the roof right now? It's unbelievable.
Has this unusually high-energy, little-sleep state felt like a distinct episode that is different from how you usually are?

Well, yeah, it definitely feels different. Like, usually I'm just, you know, normal. But lately, there are these stretches where I feel so bright and fired up, like everything is finally lining up perfectly. I was telling my brother that—he just bought a used Ford Ranger, by the way. Great truck, but the transmission slips a little in third gear. I told him he needs to check the fluid, maybe add some of that Lucas stuff. I used that in my old Honda and it ran for another fifty thousand miles. Hondas just go forever if you take care of them. 

But yeah, I feel so good and full of ideas, but then... if someone slows me down or questions what I'm doing, I just snap. Like, way harder than I mean to. I snapped at the guy at the hardware store yesterday just because he didn't know where the galvanized screws were. I mean, how do you work in a hardware store and not know that? It's like working at a diner and not knowing where the ketchup is. I love diners, though. There's this one out on Route 9 that makes the best hash browns, crispy on the outside but soft inside... anyway, yeah, I guess it is a distinct episode. I just get so irritable when people can't keep up with me right now.
During these high-energy times, have you done anything unusually risky or impulsive for you?

Risky? No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm just getting things done, you know? Like, I went out the other night to get some of that lumber I was talking about. You can actually find some decent pieces if you know where to look. There's this old lumberyard out past the county line, they leave their gates open sometimes. Not that I was taking anything, just looking. 

But I did buy a whole bunch of tools online the other night. Just put it all on the credit card. You need good tools if you're gonna build a deck right. My grandpa always said, "A cheap tool costs you twice." He had this amazing workshop in his basement. Smelled like sawdust and old oil. He built me this wooden train set when I was five. Every piece was hand-carved. You don't see craftsmanship like that anymore. Everything now is just plastic and snaps together. It's sad, really. 

But no, I haven't been doing anything crazy or risky. Just... getting ready for the projects.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Depressed? Like, down in the dumps? No, I don't really get like that. I mean, sure, everyone has a bad day here and there, but not for two whole weeks. Two weeks is a long time. You know what else takes two weeks? Curing concrete. Well, it takes 28 days to fully cure, but you gotta wait at least two weeks before you put any real weight on it. 

I learned that when I was helping my buddy pour a patio behind his place. We mixed all the bags by hand in this old wheelbarrow. My arms were killing me the next day. It's a real workout, better than any gym. I don't understand why people pay money to lift heavy things in a sweaty room when you could just do manual labor and actually build something. Plus, gyms always smell like that weird lemon disinfectant. It reminds me of the nursing home where I work. We use this industrial cleaner on the floors that smells exactly like that. It's supposed to be "spring breeze" or something, but it just smells like chemicals. 

But yeah, no, I haven't been depressed like that. I just stay busy, you know? Keep moving.
During these high-energy times, have you heard voices or felt sure of things that other people said were not true?

Well, yeah, actually... when I get in those fired-up stretches, you know, when I'm only sleeping a couple hours and making all these big plans for the deck and everything... I do hear things sometimes. Like, I'll hear people calling my name, or talking just outside the window, but when I go look, there's nobody there. It's weird, because it sounds so real. Like when you're watching a movie with surround sound and you think someone's knocking on your actual door? I bought this soundbar for my TV a few years ago, open-box deal at Best Buy. It was supposed to be missing the remote, but the remote was actually just taped to the bottom of the styrofoam. Best fifty bucks I ever spent. The bass on it is incredible. You watch an action movie and the whole living room shakes. 

But yeah, the voices aren't coming from the TV. And during those times... I also get this feeling, like I'm absolutely sure my supervisor at the nursing home is setting traps for me. Like she's intentionally moving my charts or messing with my supply cart just to make me look bad so she can fire me. I know it sounds crazy, but in the moment, I'm just positive she's out to get me. She's always been kind of sneaky, anyway. She wears these soft-soled shoes so you can't hear her coming down the hall. Reminds me of this cat my aunt used to have, Mr. Whiskers. Meanest cat you ever met. He would just wait on top of the refrigerator and swipe at your head when you walked by. Aunt Judy loved that cat, though. Fed him fancy canned tuna every single day. Tuna's gotten so expensive lately, have you noticed? Everything at the grocery store is just through the roof... but yeah, I guess I do get a little paranoid and hear things when I'm really revved up like that.
